{"claims":[{"claim_text":"DSA previously had the ability to act without imposing a course of action upon members who were uncomfortable with it.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A commitment to the democratic demands placed on society as a whole should be modeled within DSA's own structure and practices.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A democratic organization prioritizes consensus-building as a central principle of organization and governance.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"More formal rules and procedures should be used only in the case of serious disagreement, and not to stifle dissent or silence different points of view.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA’s effectiveness as a broad-based organization that encourages participation depends upon the extent to which it reflects democratic principles in its own structure.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Any DSA member should be able to draw on their own experience in similar community-based structures—from neighborhood associations to local unions—to understand and participate in DSA.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
